chunks: Al-‘Alā’ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams عليهما السلام:

Regarding a man who buys goods all together for one price, then appraises each garment according to what it is worth until it matches his capital, and sells it with murabaḥah, garment by garment, he عليه السلام said: “No, not until he makes clear to him that he only appraised it.”

key_terms.الْمَتَاعَ: goods or merchandise being bought and sold
key_terms.بِثَمَنٍ: for a price; the combined purchase price of the lot
key_terms.رَأْسِ مَالِهِ: his capital; the original amount invested
key_terms.مُرَابَحَةً: a profit-sale based on disclosure of cost and added profit
key_terms.يُبَيِّنَ: he clarifies or makes clear to the buyer
key_terms.يُقَوِّمُ: he appraises or assigns a value

ai.seo_question: Can a seller assign estimated individual costs to goods bought in bulk and then sell them as murabaḥah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on transparency in sales. If a merchant buys items in a lot for one combined price and then assigns estimated prices to individual items before selling them on a murabaḥah basis, he must disclose to the buyer that these figures are only his own appraisal and not the actual original cost of each item.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3801 - Al-'Ala narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (as), regarding a man who purchases goods altogether for a set price and then appraises each garment based on its value until it equals his capital, selling it item by item at a profit
Imam (as) said: "No, not until he clarifies to the buyer that he merely appraised it."
